core_obligations: Choose a K-injective complex I^bullet with injective terms representing K and use that its restriction to U is again K-injective, so that each derived functor in the triangle is obtained by applying the underlying functor to I^bullet (proof lines 8669-8675).
Reduce to the abelian case: it suffices to show that for an injective O_X-module I the sequence 0 -> i_*H_Z(I) -> I -> j_*(I|_U) -> 0 is short exact (proof lines 8676-8681).
Conclude exactness from the cited surjectivity of restriction of sections of an injective module together with the definitions (proof lines 8683-8684).
proof_roadmap: Use a K-injective representative with injective terms.
Observe the restriction to the complement remains K-injective.
Reduce to a short exact sequence for one injective module and invoke the cited surjectivity.
difficulty_reason: The lemma gives the sheaf-level distinguished triangle i_* R-H_Z(K) -> K -> Rj_*(K|_U) -> i_*R-H_Z(K)[1] in D(O_X) for a closed subset Z with open complement U. The proof chooses a K-injective complex with injective terms representing K, recalls that its restriction to U stays K-injective so that all three derived functors are computed from it, and thereby reduces the triangle to the short exact sequence 0 -> i_*H_Z(I) -> I -> j_*(I|_U) -> 0 for a single injective module I (proof lines 8669-8682). The exactness is then read off the cited surjectivity statement and the definitions (proof lines 8683-8684). H2: the parallel treatment of the sections triangle at S11-coh-triangle-support does not shorten this proof, and the reduction to a single short exact sequence of injective modules is the substance.
